clue.text: Without starters Eliot Ness is upset and is no longer able to manage

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
starters are the opening letters of the two names, which are dropped here

explanation.surface: The famous Prohibition agent, missing his first initials, is so agitated he can no longer cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without starters' removes E and N from ELIOT NESS, leaving LIOTESS, which 'upset' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is an idiom for losing control or composure, no longer coping.

clue.text: French king taking note of this girl

parts.note: Louis was the name of many kings of France
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A girl named after a French monarch with a musical note added.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Silly, silly dispute not finished

indicators.note: the second silly tells us the letters are behaving foolishly and get jumbled
the word dispute loses its final letter because it is cut off before its end

explanation.surface: A foolish row that never reached its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts the E off DISPUTE; 'silly' then rearranges DISPUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly are synonyms describing foolish behaviour.

clue.text: It's rising little by little, from POW camp might you say?

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp

indicators.note: you say signals that the word before it is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the word might, spoken, matches a word for a tiny creature

explanation.surface: A question about something slowly emerging from a prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave formation built upward from the floor by dripping minerals, growing very slowly over time.

clue.text: Hicks wants to talk shop about release initially, agitated and very 2

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so all the gathered letters are shaken into a new order
initially picks the opening letter of the word release

explanation.surface: A man called Hicks wants to discuss work matters regarding a release, and is flustered and very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from 'release initially' joins HICKS WANTS TO TALK SHOP, and 'agitated' rearranges all 21 letters; 'about' is a link meaning concerning. '2' points to the answer of 2 down, so 'very 2' is very silly.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom compares a dim person to two short planks of wood, meaning extremely stupid.

clue.text: Reports leading to top Australian expert getting sack

parts.note: in Australian slang a gun is someone outstandingly skilled, such as a gun shearer
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Accounts that lead to a leading Australian specialist losing their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are loud bangs, and shots from guns make such bangs.

clue.text: Lots getting a good bargain

definitions.meaning: a purchase made at a very favourable price

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a large quantity and a deal on very good terms.

clue.text: Where they make plans to travel huge distances, as article here shows up

definitions.text: Where they make plans to travel huge distances

indicators.note: in a down clue shows up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A place planning very long journeys is displayed in this item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is a link pointing to this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The US space agency plans missions that travel vast distances into space.

clue.text: Ranting foolishly about nothing, knowing no better

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram is placed around the next piece
foolishly means in a silly way, so the letters of ranting are muddled

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone ranting stupidly about nothing who simply knows no better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' turns RANTING into IGNRANT, and 'about' wraps that around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant is lacking knowledge, so not knowing any better.

clue.text: How one looks when in complete agreement

definitions.text: How one looks when in complete agreement

parts.words: How one looks when in complete agreement
parts.note: read literally, people who agree fully gaze straight at each other's faces, which is also the idiom for agreeing

explanation.definitionFit: Seeing things the same way is the idiom for full agreement between people.

clue.text: Article from France on kind of radiation used initially for part of the palate

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet radiation

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word used

parts.note: la is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A French word placed on ultraviolet rays used in treating part of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvula is the fleshy lobe hanging from the soft palate at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Basically popular city church

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Essen is a city in Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fundamentally fashionable urban place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fundamentally or at heart, which is what basically means.

clue.text: Blathering skites hiding sailor's warm clothing

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so one piece goes within the other
blathering means talking nonsense, so the letters of skites are jumbled

parts.note: Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Chattering braggarts concealing a seaman's warm garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blathering' rearranges SKITES into SKIETS, which then holds JACK. Skite is Scots and Australian for a boaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded jackets worn for skiing are warm outer garments.

clue.text: Riot involves a musical group

indicators.note: involve in its old sense means to wind or twist up, so the letters of riot are twisted around

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out among a band of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is an ensemble of three musicians.

clue.text: See 4
Not a suitable sign for the Limbless Association!

definitions.text: Not a suitable sign for the Limbless Association!

parts.words: Not a suitable sign for the Limbless Association!
parts.note: a notice restricting entry to those who belong would be tactless for a group whose people lack arms or legs

explanation.definitionFit: A notice limiting entry to those who belong to a club, with a pun on members as limbs.

clue.text: Evangelist, a twin possibly and a great writer

parts.note: Mark is one of the four Gospel writers

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among others, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Gospel author, possibly one of twins, and also a major novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A TWIN into TWAIN; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author of Tom Sawyer is ranked among the great novelists.

clue.text: 2? Certainly not like us!

definitions.meaning: the answer to 2 down, meaning silly or foolish
the setters, who write the puzzle's hints, are full of them, unlike this word

explanation.surface: A foolish person, the setter insists, is nothing like the puzzle's writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means lacking understanding, and literally without clues, unlike setters.

clue.text: A stumbling block to Basle, disunited about a century

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the next piece
disunited means broken apart, so the letters are split up and rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A barrier on the road to the Swiss city, divided around a hundred years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disunited' scrambles the seven letters into OBSTALE before 'about' wraps them round the hundred; Basle is the Swiss city Basel.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a hindrance, which is what a stumbling block is.

clue.text: Throw up, then get set to crawl out for some seafood

parts.note: to lob is to throw high into the air

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of set and crawl are scrambled

explanation.surface: Toss something high, then get ready to creep out for a seafood meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET and CRAWL into STERCLAW; 'then get' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The pincer of a large crustacean is eaten as a seafood delicacy.

clue.text: A star not to be taken lightly, as some might say

indicators.note: this phrase signals that a word is spoken and heard rather than written

parts.note: something not to be taken lightly is grave or earnest

explanation.surface: A celebrity who should be treated with gravity, as people put it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: See 4
Knocks back something coming from the East

indicators.note: coming from signals the letters are derived from the word that follows by reshaping them

explanation.surface: Downs something that arrives from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock back food or drink is to consume it quickly, so eats fits.

clue.text: Without moving anything, replaces money in cash register

parts.note: to stock a till is to replenish it, so replacing the money in it stocks it
a till is a cash register in a shop

explanation.surface: Without shifting anything, someone puts the money back in the till.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, not moving a muscle.

clue.text: Packed, as the month's about up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the month goes round the next piece
in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: Dec is short for December, here the month

explanation.surface: Ready to go, as the month is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: The month reads CED once turned by 'up', and 'about' puts it round the other piece; the surface suggests the month ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cased has been put in a box or container, which is packed.

clue.text: Leave out some of the story Naomi told

indicators.note: some of signals that only a run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Skip part of the tale that Naomi recounted.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to skip it or exclude it.

clue.text: Admit to embrace

definitions.meaning: to admit something is to include or take it in
to embrace is to take in or include as a whole

explanation.definitionFit: Encompass means to include or contain, matching both admit and embrace.

clue.text: No one returns after working — it could make you cry!

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the first one

parts.note: on means operating or working

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Nobody comes back after a shift, which might bring you to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable releases a vapour that makes the eyes water.

clue.text: Kept in bed too long, as pyjamas can be

definitions.meaning: stayed in bed later than intended

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both overslept in the morning and worn during sleep.

clue.text: Hates having doubles first — playing two sets?

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word doubles
playing suggests moving about, so the letters are rearranged
two means the word set is taken twice over

parts.note: sets read as one set, written out

explanation.surface: A tennis player loathes doubles, playing two sets first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SETSET into ETESTS after the D; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, a synonym for hates.
